section_entries.label: Exponential sums with Hecke series
section_entries.mathematical_role: Motivates spectral cancellation, formulates Conjecture 3, derives conditional consequences, discusses a transformation-formula route, and obtains a conditional Dirichlet-polynomial mean value.

unit_result_entry.title: Conjecture 3 posits square-root cancellation in unit spectral intervals
unit_result_entry.why_material: The conjecture asks an oscillatory unit-interval sum of positive central Hecke weights to save a square root over the best unweighted bound. The paper traces this hypothesis separately to optimal E₂ and eighth-moment bounds, noting an additional spectral-error step needed for the latter.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Two zeta problems reduce to the same oscillatory spectral phase
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Both E₂ and the eighth moment are expressed through short spectral sums weighted by central Hecke values. Absolute-value use of the known bound is too weak; Stirling asymptotics of the residue factor exposes an oscillatory phase, revealing that both applications demand essentially the same cancellation problem.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Motohashi’s transformation formula offers a smoothed route but not the unsmoothed target
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The author proposes embedding the unit-interval exponential sum in a spectral transformation formula with an even Gaussian-localized test function and adjustable window G. The key obstruction is explicit: progress for the Gaussian-smoothed transform would not automatically control the unsmoothed sum required by the zeta applications.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Residues of Z₂ at spectral poles expose positive central Hecke weights; unweighted estimates saturate, while Stirling analysis reveals an oscillatory phase whose square-root cancellation would simultaneously improve E₂, the eighth moment, and pointwise Z₂.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The square-root cancellation is Conjecture 3, and the route from it to all stated applications includes conditional or heuristic steps.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Spectral poles become a cancellation bottleneck

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The article distinguishes a mean-square conjecture for Z₂, a stronger pointwise Lindelöf analogue, a spectral exponential-sum conjecture, optimal moment statements, and classical RH/Lindelöf; several one-way implications are proved, but equivalence is established only for narrower reformulations.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This is a dependency map within the source, not evidence that any of Conjectures 1–3 is true.
related_synthesis_entries.title: A hierarchy of non-equivalent conjectural strengths

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Conjecture 3 asks phase rotation to save a square root in each unit spectral interval; partial summation would then adapt this primitive to both E_2 and the eighth moment.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Conjecture 3 bounds the unit-window sum of alpha_j H_j(1/2)^3 exp(i kappa_j log(kappa_j/tau)) by K^{1/2+epsilon} in a stated K/tau range. Corollary 5 conditionally derives square-root E_2 by dyadic splitting, partial summation, and Delta=T^{1/2}. Corollary 6 conditionally derives the optimal eighth moment, with an additional application to the discrete-spectrum part of Delta(T).
directed.conceptual_reading: The hypothesis targets coherence rather than coefficient size; the same cancellation primitive is reused with different outer weights.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Unit spectral sums -> subdivision/partial summation -> application formulas for E_2 and the eighth moment.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Conjecture 3 is unproved, and the eighth-moment consequence contains a separate spectral-error step; optimality is heuristic.
